competency_fulfillment.rationale: As with the parallel Grade 1 Quarter 1 ordering node, the competency requires ordering 'from smallest to largest, and vice versa', but all six widened samples, including the sort_order-formatted seed 50 ('Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 15, 5, 8'), only ever pose the ascending direction.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The descending, 'vice versa' sub-case named explicitly in the competency wording never appears across any of the six seeds, even the extra seed 50 chosen to sample the alternate sort_order formatter.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Instructions like seed 44's 'Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest: 13, 1, 14' stay to a single clear sentence with three numbers, appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sampled triples mix single- and double-digit values (e.g. seed 45's '12, 5, 10'), a meaningful structural variant that the Grade 1 Quarter 1 sibling node's narrower 1-6 pool did not show.

competency_alignment.rationale: All six samples are genuine ascending-sequence tasks that build the ordering skill directly, with no drift into an unrelated axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The largest value across all six samples, including seed 50's '15, 5, 8', is 15 -- well under the competency's stated up-to-100 ceiling, so numbers in the 16-100 band are never ordered.
